newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian stocks close higher in quiet trade.
newsitem.headline: Colombian stocks close higher in quiet trade.

text.p: Colombian stocks closed slightly higher in quiet trade as gains in Banco de Colombia and Cementos Caribe buoyed the country's leading price indexes.
Medellin's IBOMED general price index ended up 0.42 percent at 13,246.30 on a lackluster volume of 827.2 million pesos.
Bogota's IBB closed up 0.56 percent, ending at 845.90 on an even lower volume of 792.11 million pesos -- down from a daily average of more than 2.0 billion pesos so far this year.
Market movers in Bogota were led by Banco de Colombia, which ended up 2.18 percent at 445 pesos on news that its shareholders will soon approve a larger-than-expected dividend.
Other leading shares such as Banco Industrial Colombiano and Cementos Diamante closed mostly unchanged, but brewer Bavaria SA fell 0.5 percent on profit-taking to close at 3,750 pesos per share.
"The drop isn't significant," one broker said, noting the day's low trading volume.

In Medelln, volume was heavily concentrated in food-maker Industrias Alimenticias Noel, which closed unchanged at 2,750 pesos a share. Cement manufacturer Cementos Caribe was also actively traded, ending up 2.53 percent on the day at 3,900 pesos a share.
"Volumes are so low that price moves have little meaning," the Bogot-based broker told Reuters.
"Whoever invests in stocks in a big way at this point must have access to inside information," he added. "The rest is just small stuff."
